### workspace focus --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace focus [options] [project]

Bring the project's iTerm window to the front, then run the window-tool steps of the
global focus.chain (default: bare `focus`, no extra steps).
A failed step is a warning, not an error. `workspace config set focus.chain
"focus + center + dim --opacity 0.5 --duration 3"` also centers the window
and dims the others for 3 seconds. See docs/README.focus.md.
Auto-detects the project from the current directory if not specified.

Options:
        --name WS                    The project to focus, as an option (same as the positional [project])
        --shake                      Shake the window after focusing
        --highlight                  Highlight the window after focusing
        --color COLOR                Color for highlight (default: green)
                                     Colors: red, green, blue, yellow, orange, purple, white, cyan, magenta, random
        --pane PANE                  Also select this pane once the window is up front: a pane id (%19) or
                                     window.pane (0.1). Must belong to the project's tmux session
        --cycle                      Focus the next tracked project with a live window, by name, after the one in front
        --reverse                    With --cycle, go to the previous one
        --center                     Center the window on the visible area of its screen after focusing, keeping its size
        --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) instead of text, which goes to stderr

Examples:
  workspace focus    # focus the current directory's project
  workspace focus my-notes --pane %19    # focus the window and select pane %19
  workspace focus my-notes    # focus a specific project
  workspace focus --shake my-notes    # shake the window after focusing
  workspace focus --highlight my-notes    # highlight the window green (default)
  workspace focus --highlight --color blue my-notes    # highlight in another color
  workspace focus --cycle    # focus the next workspace window; repeat to keep going
  workspace focus --cycle --reverse    # go the other way
  workspace focus --center my-notes    # center the window on its screen
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace focus
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
